historicalReferences: Mosport has a rich history of close finishes, and the run to the line here has often been the scene of dramatic overtakes. Think back to Peter Gregg's domination in the Trans-Am days.
The 1977 Formula 1 race here was one of the wettest on record. A true test of driver skill and car control.
Mario Andretti scored a memorable victory here in 1977. A moment etched in the memories of Canadian motorsport fans.
Mosport has hosted some incredible battles over the years, from Can-Am to the current IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship.
The 1999 ALMS race saw a thrilling finish between the Dyson Racing Riley & Scott and the Panoz LMP-1 Roadster-S. A classic!
This track has been a proving ground for some of the greatest drivers in history. A true test of courage and skill.
Remember the Trans-Am battles of the 1970s? Mosport was a key stop on that legendary calendar.
The track layout has remained largely unchanged over the years, preserving its unique character and challenges.
Mosport has seen its fair share of drama, from high-speed accidents to last-lap passes. It's a track that demands respect.
The Can-Am era at Mosport was legendary. The sound of those big V8s echoing through the hills was something special.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this abrasive surface. Expect teams to be closely monitoring tire wear throughout the race.
The pit window here is relatively short, so teams will need to execute their pit stops flawlessly to avoid losing valuable time.
Fuel consumption will also be a concern, particularly in the closing stages of the race. Teams will need to carefully manage their fuel load.
Track position is crucial at Mosport, as overtaking can be challenging. Getting a good start and maintaining position will be key.
The long back straight offers a prime overtaking opportunity, but drivers will need to be patient and precise.
With the high speeds and challenging corners, safety car periods are always a possibility. Teams need to be prepared for any eventuality.
The 3.957km layout means shorter stints and different strategic approaches compared to longer circuits.
Managing traffic will be critical, especially for the leading cars as they navigate through slower traffic.
weatherCommentary: The weather can change quickly here in Bowmanville. Keep an eye on those clouds looming over Lake Ontario.
The wind can be a factor at Mosport, particularly on the back straight. It can affect the car's stability and braking performance.
The temperature is expected to rise throughout the day, which could impact tire grip and engine performance.
There's a chance of showers later this afternoon. If it rains, the track will become incredibly slippery and challenging.
The humidity is high today, which could make things even more difficult for the drivers inside the cockpit.
